extracted.intended_audience: short story writers, magazine editors, and anthology selectors (creative-writing / literary critics)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial/curatorial criteria for choosing and rating short stories for an annual anthology, emphasizing artistic substance, form, and literary sincerity. Includes procedural rules (coverage period, authorship limits, exclusions) and a star/asterisk rating system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of Substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The first test of a short story... is to report upon how vitally compelling the writer makes his selected facts or incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substance must be 'organic substance' — substance in which the pulse of life is beating. 'Substance is something achieved by the artist in every act of creation... a fact or group of facts in a story only attain substantial embodiment when the artist's power of compelling imaginative persuasion transforms them into a living truth.' The editor uses this as the primary test: does the material become a living truth through the writer's imaginative power?

rubrics_metrics.name: Organic vs. Inorganic Fiction (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: No substance is of importance in fiction, unless it is organic substance... Inorganic fiction has been our curse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid formulaic or 'inorganic' writing where life is not genuinely present. The editor explicitly rejects formulae and 'organized criticism' as dead; stories should not be mere formulaic constructions or vicarious wish-fulfilment that maim reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of Form
rubrics_metrics.description: A second test is necessary... The true artist will seek to shape this living substance into the most beautiful and satisfying form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form involves skilful selection and arrangement of material and the most direct and appealing presentation in portrayal and characterization. Judges should assess whether the writer has shaped substance into an aesthetically satisfying whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological and Imaginative Reality / Fresh Living Current
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection seeks 'the fresh, living current which flows through the best of our work, and the psychological and imaginative reality which our writers have conferred upon it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer stories that convey psychological truth and imaginative reality — those that feel alive, sincere, and convey essential human qualities. This is a qualitative, affective criterion: does the story pulse with life and internal truth?

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Human Qualities / 'Criticism of Life'
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor's task is 'disengaging the essential human qualities in our contemporary fiction which, when chronicled conscientiously by our literary artists, may fairly be called a criticism of life.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the story captures essential human experiences or conditions in a way that amounts to a conscientious criticism of life, rather than mere anecdote or entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping & Star/Asterisk Rating System (scoring guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are divided into four groups and indicated in the yearbook index by asterisk notation: none, one (*), two (**), three (***)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group definitions: (1) No asterisk — fail to survive either the test of substance or form (listed without comment). (2) One asterisk (*) — survives either the test of substance OR the test of form; may possess distinction of technique alone or a persuasive sense of life prompting reader response. (3) Two asterisks (**) — survives BOTH tests (substance and form); such stories may justify a second reading. (4) Three asterisks (***) / 'Rolls of Honor' — unite genuine substance and artistic form in a closely woven pattern with such sincerity they may claim a position in our literature. Additionally, some titles in the Rolls have an extra asterisk indicating a personal preference of the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-reading Criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories of still greater distinction include such narratives as may lay convincing claim to a second reading, because each of them has survived both tests, the test of substance and the test of form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'willingness to reward a second reading' as a sign of literary depth: if rereading reveals further richness, the story meets a higher standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding Personal Bias (with disclosed exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor states: 'In compiling these lists, I have permitted no personal preference or prejudice to consciously influence my judgment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for objective application of the above criteria; however, the editor allows for and discloses a limited personal preference (marked by an additional asterisk) for some titles in the Rolls of Honor — transparency about preferences is advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity and Artistic Freedom (value criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A plea for sincerity and artistic freedom: 'America's literature must no longer be the product of a child's brain in a man's body... it is because my faith in America is founded on her weaknesses as well as her strength that I make this plea for sincerity and artistic freedom.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor work that is sincere and artistically free — not pandering to commercial optimism or national myth-making; truthful confrontation of experience is preferred over wish-fulfilment or safe optimism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Distinction vs. Persuasive Sense of Life
rubrics_metrics.description: Some stories may 'survive either the test of substance or the test of form' — i.e., they may possess 'distinction of technique alone, or... a persuasive sense of life in them to which a reader responds with some part of his own experience.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize two distinct strengths: technical/ stylistic excellence (form) and a persuasive evocation of life (substance). Either can justify inclusion at a mid level; ideally both should be present for higher distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural Selection Constraints (coverage, authorship, exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules of selection and publication: selection covers stories published November 1918 to September 1919; the editor will not republish an English story nor a translation from a foreign author; rule not to include more than one story by an individual author in the volume. Order of stories in the volume is alphabetical by author and not an indication of comparative excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these administrative constraints when compiling an annual anthology: set a clear coverage period, exclude translations/foreign-language originals if policy requires, limit to one story per author to broaden representation, and make ordering/placement choices transparent (e.g., alphabetical rather than rank).

rubrics_metrics.name: Yearbook Indexing & Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that fail, survive one test, survive both, or are in the Rolls of Honor are indicated in the yearbook index with no asterisk, one, two, or three asterisks respectively; supplementary parts of the volume explain general and particular results of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain explicit documentation and indexing of selection decisions and gradations of merit; provide supplementary materials (indexes, rolls of honor, magazine averages) to justify and contextualize selections.
